lesson_title: Read a Histogram Like a Mountain Range
hook_text: 40 homework times. One glance at the graph and you know the whole story. Here's how to read it like a hiker.
clip_script: Stand each hole's count up as a peak of rock: heights 6, then 16, then 9, then 6, then 3, rising side by side along the minutes line with no valley floor showing between them — because time is continuous; 39,9 minutes touches 40 with nothing in between. What you have drawn is a mountain range. Read the range the way a hiker would. Where is the summit — the highest peak? Over the twenty-to-forties: that is where the homework times crowd. Which way do the foothills run? To the right: after the summit, the ridges step down through 9 and 6 and 3, stretching out toward the two-hour workers. Tall means many, wide means nothing.
visual_style: A histogram morphing into a rocky mountain range at golden hour, a tiny hiker figure pointing at the summit, then panning right along the descending ridge with height numbers glowing on each peak.
pacing: Bars rise one by one on a beat, morph into mountains, hold on the summit reveal, sweep right along the tail, end on the tall-means-many punchline.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to master histograms and data comments.
